title: Chinese carmakers told to improve locking devices for UK market
summary: UK insurers require critical modifications for sale in country with higher levels of car theft than China British authorities may have well-founded concerns about the cyber-spying threat from vehicles made in China, but it turns out the country’s manufacturers have security worries of their own. Insurers have told Chinese carmakers they need certain critical modifications for vehicles on British streets: namely, tougher locking devices to make them harder to steal. Continue reading...

title: Porepunkah travel warnings eased after ‘largest ever’ tactical police operation in search for Dezi Freeman
summary: More than 125 specialist officers search ‘abandoned structures, mineshafts and huts’ with Victoria police reaffirming resolve to find alleged killer Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Victorian authorities have lifted travel restrictions in the Porepunkah area, days after mounting Australia’s “largest ever” tactical policing operation to sweep the rugged bushland searching for fugitive Dezi Freeman. Suspected police killer Freeman has been sought since 26 August, when he allegedly shot and killed two officers who were executing a search warrant at his residence in Victoria’s north-east. title: A third of UK firms using ‘bossware’ to monitor workers’ activity, survey reveals
summary: Research suggests increase in office snooping in trend that some managers claim undermines trust with staff Share your experience of tech surveillance at work in the UK A third of UK employers are using “bossware” technology to track workers’ activity with the most common methods including monitoring emails and web browsing. Private companies are most likely to deploy in-work surveillance and one in seven employers are recording or reviewing screen activity, according to a UK-wide survey that estimates the extent of office snooping.
